text: The 1st Annual Streamy Awards was the first-ever awards ceremony focused exclusively on web series and marked the inaugural installment of the Streamy Awards. The event took place on March 28, 2009, at the Wadsworth Theatre in Los Angeles, California, with over 1,300 audience members in attendance and a live online broadcast. The Official Red Carpet Pre-Show was hosted by Shira Lazar, while the main award show was co-hosted by Tubefilter, NewTeeVee, and Tilzy.TV. The nominees were announced on March 13, 2009, and the finalists for the Audience Choice Award for Best Web Series were revealed on March 17. The Streamy Craft Award winners were announced on March 26, 2009, and the remaining award categories were unveiled during the main ceremony on March 28. Winners of the categories were selected by the International Academy of Web Television, except for the Audience Choice Award for Best Web Series, which was determined by public vote. The web series The Guild and Dr. Horrible's Sing-Along Blog were the top winners, taking home four and six awards, respectively, out of the 25 award categories. The event received positive reviews from celebrities and the media. Virginia Heffernan of The New York Times Magazine described it as "a goofy and a powerful experience," while Alexia Tsotsis of LA Weekly called it "an Emmys for Web TV." Maria Russo of TheWrap and Patrick Orndorff of Wired praised the quality of the nominees, with Russo noting that although the event felt "very fledgling" in the broader context, it offered "a cool glimpse into the future." Heffernan, Tsotsis, and Jill Weinberger of Gigaom highlighted the memorable speeches of Dr. Horrible's Sing-Along Blog writer Joss Whedon and The Guild star Felicia Day—Whedon commended online content creators, and Day said her awards were "for everyone who ever said no to me." YouTuber and singer Tay Zonday expressed enthusiasm, stating that the awards show that "people don't have to play the system to have their art acknowledged," and actor David Faustino remarked that they were at the "baby stage of something that's going to be amazingly giant and I'm excited to be on ground floor." Brian Lowry of Variety criticized the name, calling the Streamys the "Worst Award Name Ever."
